hypothesis: Force decodability keeps falling from N=128 to N=256 on matched seeds under the current pipeline. With seeds 22-23 on data_seed 0 (4 layers, d_model=64, e in [0, 0.5], m2 in [0.1, 1], 3000 steps, best-of-3 controls), matched to the N=64 arm (exp-20261013-011737-dff2: force 0.247/0.234) and the N=128 arm (exp-20261013-041843-8486: force 0.108/0.094), the final best-layer force margin at N=256 is lower than the same seed's N=128 value. The headroom-normalised accel_step margin stays near 0.7. Margins are read from run-record trajectories as unrounded values against a strict >= required_margin bar, with force taken at its best layer at each checkpoint. Paired differences are computed per seed from run records. If either arm's per-seed values are unavailable, the comparison is reported as not computed. N=256 values from before the pipeline change (f-20261013-000253-c709) are not used.
expected_if_true: In both seeds, the final N=256 force margin is at least 0.03 below the same seed's N=128 value (seed 22 <= 0.078, seed 23 <= 0.064). Normalised accel_step (R2 - control)/(1 - control) is in [0.60, 0.78] in both seeds.
expected_if_false: In at least one seed, the final N=256 force margin is >= that seed's N=128 value (seed 22 >= 0.108 or seed 23 >= 0.094), as in N=256 seed 20 (0.113), which exceeded N=128 seeds 22-23. Any other outcome is inconclusive.
